Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat ash-Shu'ara' (The Poets)

It is Meccan, except for four verses at the end of the surah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ta, Sin, Mim﴾. Qatadah said: it is one of the names of the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it is the name of the surah.

It is narrated from some of them that the ta is from ṭawl (bounty), the sin is from sanā' (exalted rank), and the mim is from mulk (sovereignty). Some of them said: the ta is the tree of Ṭuba, the sin is the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and the mim is Muhammad (ﷺ). It is also said: the ta is from His name al-Ṭahir (the Pure), the sin is from His name al-Salam (the Source of Peace), and the mim is from His name al-Majid (the Glorious).
And His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ — We have already explained this earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 3:

The Most High's words: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself﴾, that is: killing yourself. It is said: destroying yourself through grief.

And the Most High's words: ﴿that they will not be believers﴾, meaning: if they do not believe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 4:

His saying: ﴿If We wish, We could send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain bowed before it.﴾ Ibn Juraij said: its meaning is: We show them a matter from Our command, so that no one disobeys. And it was said: "If We wish, We send down from the sky a sign, and they are compelled to faith."

And His saying: ﴿So their necks would remain bowed before it, humbled.﴾ There are several opinions. The first: "khadi'in" (humbled) is in the sense of "khadi'a" (humbled, feminine). The second opinion: what is meant by "a'naq" (necks) is the noble and great ones among the people. According to this, the meaning of the verse is: their great and noble ones would remain humbled before the sign. The third opinion: He mentioned "the necks," and what is meant is "the owners of the necks," so the word "khadi'in" refers back to the pronoun implied in the speech.

The poet said:

﴿The passing of years has taken from me, as the crescent of the moon is taken by the dark of the night.﴾ So his saying "akhadhna" (they have taken) refers back to "al-sinin" (the years), not to his saying "marr al-sinin" (the passing of the years).

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿And there does not come to them any reminder from the Most Merciful, but that they turn away from it.﴾ That is: "muhdath" (newly revealed) means its revelation to the Prophet is recent. We have already explained this before.

And His words: ﴿except that they were turning away from it.﴾ That is: from faith.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So they have denied, but there will come to them the news of what they used to mock.﴾ That is, "there will come to them" means "they will come to them" (sawfa ya'tihim, i.e., it will surely come to them).

And His saying: ﴿the news of what they used to mock at﴾ means: the consequence (ʿāqibah) of what they used to mock at, that is, the consequence of what they used to mock. This indicates that every denier is also a mocker.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 7:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have they not looked at the earth, how many of every noble kind We have caused to grow therein?﴾ That is: of every good kind. And "zawj" (kind, pair) is like: sour and sweet, white and black, and what resembles them.

Al-Sha'bi said: "The creation are the plants of the earth. Whoever enters Paradise is noble (karim), and whoever enters the Fire is base (la'im). The Arabs say: 'a noble date palm' (nakhla karima) when its fruit is good, and 'a noble man' (rajul karim) when his conduct is good."
In the Most High's words: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾. That is: not affirming (as true).
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful﴾ — We have already explained it before.

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord called out to Moses﴾, i.e., from the right side of the mountain (al-Tur), as the Qur'an has reported; and Ibn Jubayr said: from the sky.

And His saying: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., the disbelievers."

Translation of the passage:

And His saying: ﴿The people of Pharaoh; will they not be wary?﴾ Its meaning is: will they not fear?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 12–13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I fear that they will deny me, and my chest will be constricted"﴾. It is also read "wa-yadiqu sadri" with the qaf in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: "I fear that my chest will be constricted."

And His saying: ﴿and my tongue will not be loosed﴾. He said: this refers to the knot (ʿuqda) that was on his tongue.

And His saying: ﴿so send to Aaron﴾. Its meaning: so send to Aaron along with my sending (Gabriel/the message).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I fear that they will deny me, and my chest will be constricted"﴾. It is also read "wa-yadiqu sadri" with the qaf in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: "I fear that my chest will be constricted."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿And they have a charge of sin against me﴾, meaning: a claim of a sin, and that sin is the killing of the Copt.

And His saying: ﴿So I fear that they will kill me﴾ for that man. In the story: Pharaoh had been seeking him throughout this period, to kill him for the Copt.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Kalla﴾ means: do not fear.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾ — we have already explained the interpretation of "the signs" earlier.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed We are with you, listening﴾ — He mentioned it in the plural form, while the intended meaning is two. It has also been said: "Indeed We are with you both, and with the Children of Israel, listening to what Pharaoh answers you." As for His saying ﴿listening﴾, we have already explained the like of this in what preceded, and we mentioned that He refers to Himself in the plural form in several places, as a manner of majesty and glorification.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 16:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So go to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ If it is asked: how is it that He did not say, "Indeed, we are two messengers (rasulan) of the Lord of the worlds"? The answer: the meaning of "rasul" (messenger) here is "risalah" (message).

The poet said:

(Indeed the slanderers have lied, what they understood of them was not evil, nor did I send them as a messenger (rasul).)

That is, "with a message" (risalah). Based on this, the meaning of the verse is: "Say, 'Indeed, we are one bearing the message (dhu risalah) of the Lord of the worlds.'" It is also said that His words ﴿rasul rab al-alamin﴾ (messenger of the Lord of the worlds) are, in meaning, the same as the dual: "rasul" here is used for the two.

And His saying: ﴿That you send the Children of Israel with us﴾ — meaning: send them with us to al-Sham (Greater Syria), for he had enslaved them and made them toil in all kinds of labor. And we have already explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 18:

And his saying: ﴿He said: Did we not raise you among us as a child?﴾ In the verse there is an omission; namely, that he (Musa) went and came back to Pharaoh, and invited him to God, and he answered him with this. And in the narrative: that Musa returned to Egypt wearing a woollen cloak, with his staff in his hand, and the wallet (al-mikhtal) hung from the head of the staff, containing his provisions. It is related that he came and entered his own house, and asked for Harun, and said to him: "Indeed God has sent me to Pharaoh, and has sent you with me to him too, so that we may call Pharaoh to God, the Exalted."

Then their mother came out and cried out, and said: "Indeed Pharaoh is seeking you to kill you; if you both go to him, he will kill you." But Musa did not heed her words, and the two of them went to the gate of Pharaoh at night, and knocked on the gate. The gatekeepers were alarmed and said: "Who is at the gate?" It is related that the doorkeeper looked down upon them, and said to them: "Who are you two?" Musa said: "I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds." So the doorkeeper went to Pharaoh and said: "A madman at the gate claims that he is the messenger of the Lord of the worlds." So they were left until morning, then he summoned him. In some of the narratives: they both remained for a year without being able to reach him, and then they reached him.

And his saying: ﴿He said: Did we not raise you among us as a child?﴾ In the narrative: when Musa entered upon him, and Pharaoh looked at him, he recognised him, and said: "Did we not raise you among us as a child?" i.e., a young child.

And his saying: ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life﴾ i.e., eighteen years. And some of them said: thirty years.

And His saying: ﴿And you did your deed that you did﴾, meaning: you killed the man, the one whom he had struck and killed. It is recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading as "fa'lataka" with a kasra on the fa'. And His saying: ﴿and you are among the disbelievers﴾, meaning: the ungrateful toward My favor. The poet said:

(And ingratitude is (corrupting) to the soul of the benefactor...)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He said, "I did it then, when I was among those who err."﴾ That is: I did what I did at that time. ﴿And I was among the astray﴾ That is: among the ignorant. It was also said: among the forgetful.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you, then my Lord granted me wisdom﴾, meaning: prophethood and knowledge.

And His saying: ﴿and made me one of the messengers﴾ has a clear meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 22:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And is this a favour with which you reproach me, that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?﴾ In it there are several opinions. The first: the interrogative alif is omitted, and its meaning is: "Or is it a favour with which you reproach me?" The poet said:

(Are you leaving the tribe, or are you hastening off? And what would harm you if you were to wait?)

That is: "Are you leaving the tribe, or are you hastening off?"

The second opinion: its meaning is "And that is a favour," i.e., the upbringing is a favour with which you reproach me, that you count it against me. His saying ﴿that you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ means: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel and dealt with them in base ways.

The third opinion: "And that is a favour with which you reproach me, by the upbringing." His saying ﴿that you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ means: by your enslaving the Children of Israel, you raised me and took me in charge. Its meaning: had you not enslaved the Children of Israel, I would not have come into your hands, and you would not have raised me, for there was already someone to raise me. The real meaning is the repelling of its reproach.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 23–24:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that Jibril (peace be upon him) said: "I was standing before my Lord when Pharaoh said this. I spread my wings and prepared myself to punish him, should my Lord command me. He said: 'O Jibril, only one who fears missing out hastens.'" The report is gharib (rare, with a weak or singular chain).

Know that asking about the mahiyya (the quiddity, the what-ness of a thing) is not permissible with respect to Allah, for it is a property of created beings. The proof is that Musa did not answer a question about the mahiyya. He did not say: "My Lord's color is such-and-such, He is made of such-and-such, and His scent is such-and-such." Rather, he answered by mentioning His acts, which indicate Him, saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain.﴾

Know that a question about the mahiyya is a question about the genus (jins) of a thing, and Allah the Exalted is exempt from genus. It is said that Musa's answer addressed the meaning of the question, not its literal form. The meaning of the question was: "And who is the Lord of the worlds?" He said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain.﴾

The meaning of His words ﴿if you are certain﴾ here is: that you are certain as you are certain of the things you [observe directly], so be certain that the God of creation is Allah the Exalted.

The Most High's saying: ﴿He said to those around him, "Do you not listen?"﴾ means: "Do you not listen?" Pharaoh said this in astonishment at Musa's (peace be upon him) answer. Those people used to believe that their gods were their kings. So Musa (peace be upon him) elaborated further in the explanation, and said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 26, verses 27–30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is certainly insane."﴾ It was their view that whoever does not hold the belief they hold is not rational, so Musa (Moses) elaborated further in the explanation, saying: ﴿"Lord of the east and the west and whatever is between them, if you were to use reason."﴾ Then Fir'awn (Pharaoh) responded and said: ﴿"If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among those imprisoned."﴾

In the narrative: his imprisonment was harsher than killing, for he would confine a man alone in a place where he could hear nothing and see nothing, and he would be cast down into the earth. Musa replied and said: ﴿"Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ That is: you would imprison me even if I bring you something clear, meaning a clear sign.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 31–32:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful." So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clearly visible serpent.﴾ The tha'ban (serpent) is the male of the snakes, the great one among them. If it is said: Did He not say in another place: ﴿as if it were a jann﴾, and the jann is the small snake? The answer to this is that the meaning of the jann is that it was like a small snake in its quivering and the manner of its movement, while in itself it was a great snake.

Al-Suddi and others mentioned that the staff became a yellow, raging snake, as great as any snake could be.

In the narrative: it rose from the ground to the height of a mile, opened its mouth wide, stood up on its tail, and began to coil (tamalmul) before the face of Pharaoh.

It is also related that it seized the dome of Pharaoh between its fangs, and Pharaoh cried out, "O Musa, I adjure you by the One who sent you!"

As for His words, ﴿clearly visible﴾ (mubin), it means that the serpent makes clear that it is a great proof.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 35:

His saying: ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic﴾. If someone says: Moses only wanted to bring the Children of Israel out, not to drive out Pharaoh and his people. The answer to this is: they had made the Children of Israel slaves and servants, so when Moses wanted to bring the Children of Israel out, it was as if he wanted to drive them out.

And his saying: ﴿So what do you command?﴾ That is: what do you advise?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: (Arjihi wa akhahu) meaning: postpone his matter and the matter of his brother. Its meaning: the decision of the matter is not complete until the proof against him becomes manifest to you.

And His saying: ﴿And send into the cities gatherers,﴾ we have already explained it.

And His words: ﴿They will bring you every skilled sorcerer who has knowledge﴾, meaning: a skilled sorcerer. In the story, it is related that he (Pharaoh) would pay stipends to the sorcerers, and he gathered six thousand sorcerers. It is also said: twelve thousand.
"And His saying: ﴿So the magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day﴾, and it is the Day of Adornment, as we have explained earlier."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 41:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿When the magicians came﴾, meaning to Musa, ﴿they said to Pharaoh: "Will there indeed be a reward for us if we are the victors?"﴾.

Their words: ﴿He said, "Yes, and indeed you will then be among those brought near."﴾ That is, in rank. And in the narrative, Musa said to the chief of the sorcerers: "Will you believe in me if I defeat you?" The chief of the sorcerers said to him: "If you are a sorcerer, then we will surely defeat you, and if you defeat us, we will surely believe in you."

God's words: ﴿Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾

And His words: ﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs, and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are surely the victorious."﴾ That is: by the might of Pharaoh and his kingdom. ﴿Indeed, we are the victorious.﴾

God's words: ﴿Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾

And His words: ﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs, and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are surely the victorious."﴾ That is: by the might of Pharaoh and his kingdom. ﴿Indeed, we are the victorious.﴾

In the narrative: all the earth, mile upon mile, became serpents and vipers in the sight of the people. When Moses cast down his staff, it became a great serpent, and it began to grow to the size of their ropes and staves. Then it kept seizing and swallowing them one by one until it had devoured them all. Then Moses took hold of its tail, and it became a staff again just as it had been. At that, the magicians were bewildered, and they said: "If this is magic, where have our staves and ropes gone?" They became certain that what Moses had brought was a command from God, so they fell down prostrating and believed. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then the magicians were thrown down, prostrating.﴾
And his saying, ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrating﴾, may mean: they fell prostrate. It may also mean: the truth that they saw cast them down prostrating (ساجدين.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds"﴾. Regarding the story: when they (the magicians) said this, Pharaoh said, "I am the lord of the worlds," and the magicians said: ﴿"The Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾

His words, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds"﴾. Regarding the story: when they (the magicians) said this, Pharaoh said, "I am the lord of the worlds," and the magicians said: ﴿"The Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 49:

And His saying: ﴿He said, "Have you believed in him before I give you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic. So you are going to know."﴾ Meaning: you are going to know the outcome of your affair.

And His saying: ﴿Surely I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all together.﴾ We have already explained its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 50:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They said: "No harm (la darar)"﴾, meaning: no harm and no disliked thing.

The poet said:

(And you, after a year, will not harm yourself... whether your mother was a gazelle or a donkey)

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾, meaning: we are going back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 51:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾, i.e., our misdeeds (dhunub).

﴿That we were the first of the believers﴾. Al-Farra' said: "the first of the believers" means the first of the people of our time. Al-Zajjaj said: "This is weak, because the Children of Israel had already believed in Musa before them. Rather, its meaning is: that we were the first of the believers at the manifestation of this proof (hujjah). It is also possible that its meaning is: that we were the first of the believers from the people of Pharaoh."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 52:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, "Travel by night with My servants"﴾. He mentioned "travel by night" (asri) because they traveled at night.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾ means: Fir'awn and his people will pursue you. It is related from 'Amr ibn Maymun that he said: When it reached Fir'awn that Musa and his people had set out, he said to his people, "When the rooster crows, mount up." But no rooster crowed that night, until Musa and his people had passed on. When it was morning, he called for a sheep and ordered it slaughtered. Then he said, "This sheep shall not be skinned until five hundred thousand fighting men have gathered." He said: The skinner had not finished skinning it before five hundred thousand fighting men had gathered, in number.

Another scholar mentioned that the angels entered the houses of the Copts and killed their firstborn sons, so they were occupied on that morning with burying the firstborn.

Almighty God's words: ﴿Then Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities, gathering [the people]﴾. He means: Pharaoh sent the police (al-shurṭ) into the cities until they gathered the people. In the books of tafsir it is said that there were a thousand cities and twelve thousand villages.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 54:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band (shirdhimah qalilun)﴾, meaning: a small group (jama'ah qalilah). They recited verses of poetry regarding the word shirdhimah:

(The winter has come, and my shirt is in tatters... the shirdhim, whom the she-camels mock at me.)

And they recited, regarding His saying ﴿qalilun﴾ (few):

﴿So he drove away the remote ones of the tribes from among them, and they returned like a single tribe of ours.﴾

Meaning: like one tribe.

And it is related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that Musa was among six hundred thousand and seventy thousand, so Fir'awn called them a shirdhimah because of the greatness of his people's numbers.

And it is related that Haman was at its vanguard with a million thousand, and it is related that Fir'awn was with seven thousand thousand, and it is related that before him were one hundred thousand archers (nashib), one hundred thousand bearers of spears (ashab al-hirab), and one hundred thousand bearers of staffs (ashab al-a'madah).

And His words, ﴿And indeed they are enraging us﴾ — meaning: they have enraged us and provoked our anger. Their provoking him was by their departure without his command, and by their borrowing the ornaments from his people and setting out with them.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 26, verse 56:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, we are all vigilant (ḥādhirūn)﴾. It is also read as "ḥadhirūn". Al-ḥadhr (caution) is the one who is alert, and al-ḥādhir is the one who is prepared and ready.

The poet said:

(And death wrote upon him, "Beware of death" ... alone, so no one remained vigilant.)

Ibn Abi 'Amir recited: "wa-innā la-jamī'un ḥādhirūn" with a non-dotted ḍāl (i.e., ﴿ḥadirūn﴾). It is said: "ba'īr ḥādir" when the camel is full of flesh and large in body. It was also said: ﴿innā la-jamī'un ḥādhirūn﴾ means "equipped" (mu'addūn), and the meaning of mu'addūn is al-adāt (the tools) and the weapons.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾. In the narrative (al-qissa): the orchards extended along both banks of the Nile from its upper course to its end. It is related from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As that he said: "The lord of the rivers is the Nile. When Allah the Exalted sends it flowing, He supplies it from all the rivers and causes the springs of the earth to gush forth for it. When its flowing is complete, every water returns to its source."

And [We bequeathed] ﴿treasures﴾, that is, treasures of wealth. In some accounts it is related that Pharaoh had eight hundred thousand servant-boys, each boy on a horse of noble breed (ʿatīq), and around the neck of each horse was a collar of gold.

And [He said]: ﴿and a noble station﴾, that is, fine dwellings. It has also been said that the noble station is the pulpits (manābir), and there were a thousand pulpits in Egypt at that time. It has also been said: ﴿and a noble station﴾ means the assembly of the nobles. Some of them mentioned that when he sat upon his throne, three hundred golden chairs were placed before him on which the nobles would sit, wearing robes of brocade (aqbiya al-dībāj) embroidered with gold.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 26, verse 59:

And His saying: ﴿Thus. And We made the Children of Israel inherit it.﴾ It is related that the Children of Israel returned to Egypt and remained there, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We made the Children of Israel inherit it.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 60:

And His saying: ﴿Then they pursued them at sunrise﴾, meaning: at the rising of the sun. Its shurūq (sunrise) is its ṭulū' (rising).

Abū Burda narrated from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī that the Prophet (ﷺ) stayed at the house of a Bedouin during a journey, and the Bedouin treated him with excellent hospitality. When he departed from him, he said to the Bedouin: "If you were to come to us, we would honour you." Afterwards the Bedouin came to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What is your need?" He said: "A she-camel with its saddle, and another that I may milk." So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that this be given to him. Then he said: "Is one of you incapable of being like the old woman of the Children of Israel?" He was asked about that, and he said:

When Mūsā (Moses) brought the Children of Israel out of Egypt, they lost the way. In some reports: the moon was eclipsed, the sun was darkened, the people fell into a great darkness, and Mūsā was bewildered. The scholars of the Children of Israel said to him: "Yūsuf (Joseph), peace be upon him, had enjoined that when the Children of Israel leave Egypt, they should carry his bones with them." Mūsā realised that they had lost the way because of this, and he said to them: "Who knows the place of his bones?" They said: "None knows it except an old woman of the Children of Israel." So he called for the old woman and asked her about the place of the bones. She said: "Not until you fulfil my need." He said: "What is your need?" She said: "My need is that I be with you in Paradise, that is, in your rank." Mūsā disliked that, so revelation came down: "Give her that." So he gave it to her. Then she guided them to the grave of Yūsuf, and Mūsā carried the bones of Yūsuf, and the darkness cleared.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 61:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So when the two hosts saw each other﴾ means: the two hosts met. The meaning of "meeting" (talaqi) is that each saw the other, this group seeing that group and that group seeing this group.

As for His words: ﴿The companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken"﴾ (mudrikun, with the shadda), the meaning is the same as what we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Never! Indeed, He said﴾ — meaning: Desist from this speech and do not say it, for they will not overtake you.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ — its meaning: indeed, my Lord is with me by protection and support.

And His saying: ﴿He will guide me﴾ — meaning: He will direct me to the path of salvation, and guidance (al-hidayah) is indeed the indication (al-dalalah) to the path of salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 63:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Then We revealed to Moses: Strike the sea with your staff﴾. In the narrative (al-qissa): a believer from the people of Pharaoh (mu'min Al Fir'awn) was in front of the Children of Israel, and he said to Moses: "O Prophet of God, where has your Lord commanded you?" He said: "In front of you." He said: "O Prophet of God, in front of me is the sea?" ﴿﴾ Moses said: "By God, you have not lied, nor has he lied."

It is related that Yusha' ibn Nun said to Moses: "O Prophet of God, where has your Lord commanded you?" He said: "The sea." He said: "Shall I plunge into it?" He said: "Yes." So he plunged into the sea and crossed. When the Children of Israel came and plunged in, they were submerged in the sea. God then revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."

It is also related that Moses plunged into the sea, but the current turned him back. So he said to the sea: "Split!" but it did not split. God Most High then commanded him to strike it with the staff. He struck it the first time, and it became muddied (fa-atta al-bahr); then he struck it a second time, and it became muddied; then he struck it a third time, and it split. This is the meaning of the words of God Most High: ﴿and it split﴾.

And His words: ﴿so every part was like a great mountain﴾ means: every split (firq) was like a cleft (falq), and firq and falq are one and the same.

And His words: ﴿like a great mountain﴾ means: like a great mountain (jabal 'azim). The poet said:

(They alighted at Abaqra, over which flows / water of the Euphrates coming from its mountains)

The narration is that the water of the sea piled up upon itself until it became like a mountain, and twelve paths appeared, and the wind dried them until they were dry, and each tribe passed along one path. They said: "We do not see our brothers, and perhaps our brothers have drowned." So God made for them openings (kuwa, plural of kuwwa) in the water, until some of them could see others, and they began to converse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 64:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We brought near the others there﴾. "Azlafna" means: We brought near. The poet said:

(So every day that passed, or night that elapsed, in it the souls draw near to their appointed terms.)

And another said:

(The nights fold up, one after another, until the crescent's halo has bent and curved.)

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Azlafna" means: We gathered. From it comes "Laylat al-Muzdalifa," meaning the night of gathering. Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "wa-azlafnahum al-akhirin" (And We brought the others near to them), meaning: We placed them in a position of nearness.

In the narrative: Jibril was between the Children of Israel and Pharaoh and his people. He would drive the Children of Israel forward, and they would say: "We have not seen a driver better at driving than this man." And he would hold back the people of Pharaoh, and they would say: "We have not seen a restrainer better at restraining than this one." It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "People must have a wazi'a (restraining force), meaning a ruler who restrains them."

We have already explained that Jibril was on a female horse in heat, and Pharaoh was on a stallion. Jibril, peace be upon him, entered the sea, and Pharaoh followed him, not controlling himself. When all of them had entered the sea, and the first of them wanted to exit while the last of them had entered, the sea closed over them. The distance between the two shores of the sea was [four] farsakhs. This is the Sea of Qulzum (the Red Sea), a part of the Persian Sea.

It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the sea had been calm before that. When Musa struck it with the staff, it became agitated, and began to surge and recede.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 65–66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We delivered Moses and all who were with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others﴾. The meaning is apparent, and al-ighraq (drowning) is destruction by submersion in water.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 65–66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We delivered Moses and all who were with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others﴾. The meaning is apparent, and al-ighraq (drowning) is destruction by submersion in water.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, meaning: a lesson (ʿibrah).

And His saying: ﴿and most of them were not believers﴾, meaning: not affirmers of the truth (mu'ammidīn). What is intended by them is the people of Pharaoh. It is narrated that none of the people of Pharaoh believed except Āsiyah, his wife, and Ḥizqīl, and the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, and the old woman who guided (them) to the bones of Joseph.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾. Al-'Aziz (the Mighty) is the Capable One whom no one can overpower (mu'azzah), meaning: none can overcome Him (mughalabah). God, exalted is He, is Mighty (ʿAziz), and in describing His might He is Merciful (Rahim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 26, verses 69–70:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham, when he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾. Its meaning: "What is it that you worship?!"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 26, verses 69–70:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham, when he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾. Its meaning: "What is it that you worship?!"

The words of the Most High: ﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ That is: we persist in worshipping them. It is said: "So-and-so continued doing such-and-such," meaning he persisted in doing it during the day.

"And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Do they hear you when you call?"﴾ Its meaning: Do they hear your voice and your supplication? And it was recited in the irregular (shadh) reading: "Do they hear you" with the yāʾ vowelled with a ḍamma (raising)."

And His saying: ﴿Or do they benefit you?﴾ That is: with provision (rizq).

And His saying: ﴿Or do they harm you?﴾ That is: they harm you if you abandon their worship.

"They said, 'Rather, we found our fathers doing thus.'" Its meaning: these (idols) do not hear our words, nor do they bring us any benefit, nor do they ward off any harm from us; but we followed our fathers. The people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) derived from this that taqlid (blind imitation) is not permissible.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 75–76:

His saying: ﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones?"﴾ That is: the earlier ones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 75–76:

His saying: ﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones?"﴾ That is: the earlier ones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 77:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed they are enemies to me﴾, meaning: enemies to me.

His saying: ﴿except the Lord of the worlds﴾. Opinions differ regarding this. One of the two opinions is that they used to worship idols alongside Allah, the Exalted, so Ibrahim said: everything you worship is an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds. The second opinion is that this is an exception of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), as if he said: "Indeed they are an enemy to me, but the Lord of the worlds is my friend (waliyy)." If it is said: how can idols be enemies to Him when they are inanimate objects, and enmity is only found in a living, rational being?

The answer to this: they said: this is from the inverted expression (al-maqlub), and its meaning is: "Indeed I am an enemy to them." It is also permissible that its meaning be: "Indeed they are an enemy to me," that is: I do not place my hopes in them, nor do I seek benefit from their direction, just as an enemy is not befriended and benefit is not sought from him.
Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ — i.e., He directs me to the path of salvation.

"And the One who feeds me and gives me drink." Its meaning: He provides me with food and drink. The real sense is that my food and my drink come from Him, and my provision comes from Him. Some of the masters of inner meditations (ashab al-khawatir) have said: He feeds me the food of affection (al-mawaddah), and gives me drink from the cup of love (al-mahabbah). It has also been said: He feeds me the taste of faith (dhawq al-iman), and gives me drink through the acceptance of obedience (qubul al-ta'ah).

And His saying, ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) mentioned this because they used to see illness as coming from foods and cure as coming from medicines. His saying, ﴿And when I am ill﴾, is the use of courtesy (adab). Otherwise, the one who causes illness and the one who cures is Allah, the Exalted, by the consensus of the people of religion (ijma' of the people of religion). Some of the companions of the spiritual insights (ashab al-khawatir) said: "And when I am ill with fear, He cures me with hope." It was also said: "When I am ill with greed, He cures me with contentment."

And His words: ﴿And who will cause me to die﴾ meaning: will cause me to die in this world, [and] will bring me to life in the Hereafter. Some of the people of inner inspirations (ahl al-khawatir) said: He causes me to die through seeing creation, and brings me to life through witnessing the Truth. And it has been said: He causes me to die through sin and brings me to life through obedience.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 26, verse 82:**

And His saying: ﴿And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense﴾. That is: I hope that He will forgive me my errors (khataya). His errors (of Abraham) are what we have mentioned of his three lies. Know that the prophets are protected (ma'sum) from the major sins (kaba'ir), but as for the minor errors (khata'ya) and minor sins (saghair), they may occur from them.

And His saying: ﴿the Day of Recompense﴾: that is, the Day of Reckoning. Muslim mentioned in his Sahih, on the narration of 'A'isha, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abdullah ibn Jud'an used to feed the guest, carry the burdened, and she mentioned some acts of goodness. Is he in Paradise or in the Fire?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He is in the Fire, for he never once said: 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense.'"

Almighty and Exalted God's words: ﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom﴾ — that is, knowledge and understanding; and it has been said: hitting upon the truth.

And His words: ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾ — that is, among the prophets and the messengers.

And His saying: ﴿And make for me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾ — that is, a good reputation until the Hour arises. It is also said that what is meant by it is that all the people of the religions should be devoted to him, and that all people should accept him. It is also said that its meaning is: place among my descendants those who will uphold the truth until the Hour arises.
and His saying: ﴿And make me of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾, that is: among those whom You give the Garden of Bliss.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 86:

And His saying: ﴿And forgive my father, for indeed he was among the misguided.﴾ The scholars said: this was before he disassociated himself from him and became certain that he was an enemy of Allah, as we mentioned in Surah al-Tawbah. Some of them said: "And forgive my father" means: his offence against me, as if he had waived his right and pardoned him.

And it is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, will cling to his father on the Day of Resurrection and say: "O Allah, forgive him, and fulfil for me what You promised me." Then Allah will transform his father's form into the form of a hyena (dhab'a), a foul and ugly thing. When Ibrahim sees him, he will abandon him and say: "This is not my father."

And His saying: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected﴾, meaning: do not expose me to shame, and that would be by not forgiving my sin; and everyone whom Allah does not forgive has indeed been disgraced by Him.

"And His saying: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾. Most scholars said: "Sound" means free from shirk, for a human being is never free from sin. It was also said: "sincere" (mukhlis). It was said: "sincere counsel-giver" (nasih). And it was said: a heart in which there is "There is no god but Allah."

"And His saying: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾. Most scholars said: "Sound" means free from shirk, for a human being is never free from sin. It was also said: "sincere" (mukhlis). It was said: "sincere counsel-giver" (nasih). And it was said: a heart in which there is "There is no god but Allah."

And His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing﴾, meaning: brought close. It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Paradise is closer to any one of you than the thong of his sandal, and the Fire is likewise."

And His saying: ﴿And the Hellfire will be brought forth﴾, i.e., the Hellfire will be made manifest.

﴿for the deviators﴾, i.e., for the disbelievers. The ghawi (deviator) is one who has fallen into a loss with no hope of recovery therein.

And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you, or can they help themselves?"

That is, "Can they ward off the punishment from you?"

And His saying, ﴿Or can they help themselves?﴾ means: can they defend themselves?

And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you, or can they help themselves?"

That is, "Can they ward off the punishment from you?"

And His saying, ﴿Or can they help themselves?﴾ means: can they defend themselves?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 94:

And His saying: ﴿Then they will be thrown headlong into it, they and those who went astray.﴾ Al-Qutaybi said: "Some of them were cast down upon others." It has also been said: they were rolled over (dahwarū), tumbled (dahdahū), and dahdadū; and it has been said: they were overturned into it. It is also said: originally it was kabbabū, and a kāf was inserted into it, so it became kabkabū.

And His saying: ﴿they and those who went astray﴾: that is, the devils along with them. It is also said: those who followed them in polytheism.
and His saying: ﴿And the hosts of Iblis, all of them﴾ means: his offspring.
His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, while they dispute therein﴾, meaning: some of them argue with one another.
"And His saying: ﴿By Allah, we were indeed in clear error﴾ means: in plain mistake."
And His saying: ﴿When we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾. This is their saying to the idols, and its meaning: we make you equal to the Lord of the worlds.
And His words: ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾ — meaning: the leaders. It is also said: Iblis and the disbelieving son of Adam, who is Qabil (Cain).

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾. In the reports (al-akhbar): that the believers intercede for the sinners, and likewise the angels and the prophets.

And (the verse says): ﴿Nor a close friend.﴾ That is, a special friend. It is also said: a near friend. He was called "ḥamīm" (close friend) because he is concerned for you (yaḥummu lak) and becomes angry on your behalf. It is related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he said: "Acquire many believing friends, for they will have intercession on the Day of Resurrection." The ṣadīq (true friend) is the one who is truthful in affection on the condition of religion. In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ), narrated through Jābir: "A believer will enter Paradise and say: 'Where is my friend so-and-so?' It will be said: 'He is in the Fire because of his sins.' So he will intercede for him, and Allah will bring him out of the Fire through his intercession."

And His saying: ﴿If only we had a return (karra)﴾, meaning: a return (raj'a) [to the world].

And His saying: ﴿so that we would be among the believers﴾: "And if we were believers, then we would have intercessors too, just as the believers have intercessors."
And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ We have already explained the meaning of all of it.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers.﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Noah was the first messenger whom God Almighty sent. This is to be understood as meaning that he was the first messenger God sent after Adam, may the blessings of God be upon him, and he was a bearer of a sharia (sharīʿa, a revealed body of law). The plural "the messengers" is mentioned because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers.

And His words, ﴿When their brother Noah said to them﴾, mean that he was their brother by lineage.

And His words, ﴿Will you not be wary?﴾, i.e., will you not fear God?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 107:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾ means: trustworthy in what is between you and between Allah, the Exalted. In some of the exegetical works it is related that Noah was called "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy) before Allah sent him.
"And His saying: ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾. That is: fear God by abandoning polytheism, and obey me in what I command you [with]."

And His saying: ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾, meaning: any reward (ju'l).

And His saying: ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: my reward. The people of knowledge said: It is not permissible for the Prophet to take a wage (ju'l) for prophethood, because that would lead to the people being repelled from accepting faith; but it is permissible for him to accept a gift (hadiyyah), because that does not lead to repulsion.
"And His saying: ﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾ — he repeated it for emphasis."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you when the lowest of people follow you?"﴾ In the exegesis: they are the weavers, the cuppers, the cobblers, and those like them. It was also said: they are the lowest of the people.

Almighty God's words: ﴿And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: Crafts do not affect religious faiths. The meaning of Noah's words is that I have no knowledge of their trade; rather, I was commanded only to call them to God, so whoever responds, I accept him. This is the meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verses 113–115:

The difference between ʿajamī (ʿajamī) and aʿjamī (aʿjamī) is that ʿajamī is the one who is attributed to the ʿAjam (the non-Arab peoples), even if he is eloquent, while aʿjamī is the one who does not speak Arabic clearly, even if he is an Arab. ʿAbd Allah ibn Muṭīʿ said concerning His saying ﴿upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: "Upon my beast." Its meaning is that if the beast had spoken, they would not have believed. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant is some of the ʿAjam, i.e., that the Qur'an was sent down in a language other than Arabic.
And His saying: ﴿Then he recited it to them, they would not have believed in it﴾ means: they did not believe.

Almighty God's words: ﴿Thus We let it enter into the hearts of the guilty.﴾ Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: We caused polytheism (shirk) to enter into their hearts. And it is said: We caused denial (takdhib) to enter into their hearts.

And His saying: ﴿They will not believe in it﴾, i.e., in the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿until they see the painful punishment﴾, i.e., at the descent of the calamity (al-ba's).

And His saying: ﴿So it will come upon them suddenly﴾, i.e., unexpectedly.

And His saying: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, i.e., they do not know.
And His saying: ﴿Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?"﴾ That is: will we be given respite (mu'akhkharun)?

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ It is related that when these verses were revealed, they said: "When will this punishment be?" or "Bring us this punishment," so God Most High revealed: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 26, verse 205:

Regarding the words of the Most High, ﴿Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years﴾, Ikrimah said: [it refers to] the lifespan of the world. And it is related from Shurayk ibn Abd Allah al-Nakha'i that he said: it is forty years. But most of the commentators hold that there is no specific figure in it; rather, what is meant is many years. And al-Imta' (enjoyment) is living in what is pleasant and desired.
Then there came to them what they had been promised. That is, the punishment.
And His saying: ﴿What did what they were enjoying avail them?﴾ That is: their livelihood and their enjoyment of the world did not avert the punishment from them.
The Most High's saying: ﴿We never destroyed a town but it had warners.﴾ This is in the sense of His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We had sent a messenger.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 209:

And His saying: ﴿A reminder﴾, meaning: We sent the warners (al-Mundhirun) as a reminder for them.

And His saying: ﴿And We were never wrongdoers﴾, its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 210:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿And the devils have not brought it down.﴾ The polytheists used to say: "Indeed, a devil descends upon Muhammad (ﷺ) and teaches him the Qur'an." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And His saying: ﴿And it is not befitting for them﴾, meaning: it is not suitable for them that they should bring down the Qur'an, because they are not people deserving of that.

And His saying: ﴿nor are they able to do it﴾, meaning: they are not able to bring down the revelation.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing [the heavenly message]﴾, meaning: [they are veiled off]. For they were barred from the heaven and kept away by the meteors, as we have mentioned before.

God's words: ﴿So do not invoke another god alongside God, lest you be among those punished.﴾ It is related that the polytheists said to him: "Return to the religion of your fathers. If you want wealth, we will gather wealth for you; and if you want leadership, we will make you our leader." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿So do not invoke another god alongside God, lest you be among those punished.﴾ That is: in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 214:

The Almighty's words: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾. Al-Zuhri narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab [and Abu] Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Abu Hurayrah, that when the words of the Almighty ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ were revealed, the Prophet said: "O assembly of Quraysh, buy yourselves from Allah, for I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Banu Abd Manaf, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah bint Muhammad, ask me from my wealth whatever you wish, but I cannot avail you anything against Allah." He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This was reported to us by al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq, who said: my grandfather informed us, al-Firabri informed us, al-Bukhari informed us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri... the report.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ascended al-Safa and then said: "Yaa sabaahaah!" So Quraysh gathered around him and said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I told you that an enemy was about to attack you at morning or evening, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! Is it for this that you called us?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾. The report is in the two Sahihs.

In some reports: the Prophet said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Gather for me the Banu Abd Manaf." So he gathered them around a shank of a sheep and a bowl of milk. When they had eaten and drunk, the Messenger of Allah said to them what he said and invited them to Allah. Then Abu Lahab stood up and said what we have mentioned, and they left.

In the Tafsir of al-Naqqash: the Prophet singled out the Banu Hashim and the Banu Abd al-Muttalib with the invitation and said: "You are my close family."
And His saying: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾ — meaning: soften your side (toward them) and be good in your character.
And His saying: ﴿But if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful﴾. In the codices of the people of Medina and the Syrians, it is "fatawakkal" (fa-tawakkal) with the fa'. The fa' in it carries the meaning of a consequence (al-jaza'), and the sense of that is: if they disobey, then meet their disobedience with reliance upon Me."

His saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: when you stand to call them (to faith) and to recite the Qur'an to them. It is also said: when you rise from your sleep to pray. And it is said: when you pray alone.

And His words: ﴿and your turning about among those who prostrate﴾ [meaning:] when you pray in congregation. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding its meaning that he said: "He brought him forth from the loins of one prophet to the loins of another prophet, thus, until He made him a prophet. This is the meaning of the turning." And "those who prostrate" are the prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all. And it is related from Mujahid that he said: the meaning of His words ﴿and your turning about among those who prostrate﴾ is the turning of the gaze, and he would see behind him just as he saw in front of him.
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ — its meaning is apparent.
God's words, "Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?" (Qur'an 26:221): meaning, "Shall I tell you?" And this is an answer to their saying that a devil descends upon him (the Prophet ﷺ).

The Qur'an verse quoted: ﴿Upon every lying, sinful one they descend﴾ — the system prompt says to keep the ﴿ ﴾ markers and translate the meaning plainly inside them.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿They descend upon every lying, sinful one﴾. Meaning: they descend (tatanazzal). The affak (أفاك) is one who lies excessively, and the athim (أثيم) is one who commits what makes him sinful and whose action is ugly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 223:

The word of God Most High: ﴿They cast [what they hear] by hearing﴾. The people of tafsir said: what is meant by this is the soothsayers (kuhhan), and the meaning of ﴿they cast the hearing﴾ is that they listen to the devils.

And His word: ﴿and most of them are liars﴾, meaning, all of them. It is related from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, the soothsayers tell of things and they turn out to be true?" He said: "That is a snatched word which the jinn snatches and drops into the ear of the soothsayer, and he mixes with it a hundred lies."

We have already mentioned that they eavesdrop on the angels, and some of them climb over others, and then they are pelted with shooting stars.

And in the well-known, widely transmitted report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes to a soothsayer or a diviner (ʿarrāf) and believes him in what they say, has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 224:

The word of the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them.﴾ The people of tafsir said: What is meant by "the poets" are the poets who used to satirize the Muslims from among the disbelievers and revile the Prophet (ﷺ), such as ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zibaʿrā, Abū ʿIzza al-Jumahī, Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Hubayra ibn Wahb, and those resembling them.

As for the word of the Exalted: ﴿those who go astray follow them﴾, there are several opinions concerning it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: they are the reciters (al-ruwāh). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from him that the meaning of the verse is that the poet and his rival trade insults, so one group follows this one and another group follows that one.

It is narrated from Mujāhid that "those who go astray" are the devils (shayāṭīn). And from some of them: they are the foolish among the people.

In the reports it is stated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever walks seven steps toward a poet is among those who go astray." And the report is gharīb (weak/strange in its chain).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 26, verse 225:

The Most High's saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they wander in every valley?﴾ That is: they are led astray (yuftanun) every time. The mention of "valley" is by way of illustration. It is said: "I am in a valley, and you are in a valley." It is reported from Qatadah that he said: "wandering in every valley" means that they praise falsely and disparage falsely. Some of them said: the poet praises for a reward (al-silah), satirizes out of partisanship (al-hamiyyah), composes amatory verses about women (yatashabbab bi'l-nisa'), and his lover stirs his thoughts. Others said: regarding ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, "every valley they wander" means: they compose rhymes (yasughun al-qawafi) according to one of the letters of the alphabet (harf min huruf al-hija'). The haim (one who wanders) is the one who abandons the right course (al-qasd) in matters. It is said: "Fulan wandered (hama) in his direction" when he has no correct goal (maqsid sahih) that he aims for and goes toward.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 226:

His saying: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾, meaning: they lie in their poetry, and they say, "We did such-and-such," when they did not do it. And in some reports: Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi composed a poem in which he confessed to drinking wine, so 'Umar wanted to impose the hadd (the prescribed legal punishment) on him. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed, the Book of Allah averts the hadd from him," and he recited this verse: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾. So 'Umar left off his hadd.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 26, verse 227:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. The people of tafsir said: These are the poets among the Muslims who used to avoid the poets of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), satirize them, defend the Prophet and his Companions, and retaliate on their behalf. They are such as Hassan ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Rawahah, Ka'b ibn Malik, and those like them.

And ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik narrated from his father that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about poetry?" He said: "Indeed the Muslim strives with his hand and his tongue. By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is as if you were shooting them with arrows."

And Shuʿbah narrated from ʿAdi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, that the Prophet said to Hassan ibn Thabit: "Satirize them – or satirize them, and Ruh al-Qudus is with you." It was mentioned by al-Bukhari in [the chapter on] ﴿And they remember Allah much and defend themselves after being wronged﴾ in the Sahih. He (al-Sam'ani) said, may Allah be pleased with him: "This was related to us by al-Makki ibn ʿAbd al-Razzaq, who said: my grandfather related to me, al-Firabri related to us, al-Bukhari related to us, Hafs ibn ʿUmar related to us from Shuʿbah... the report."

And from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "Poetry is speech; some of it is good and some of it is ugly. Take the good and leave the ugly."

And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated from the Prophet that he said: "Indeed, some poetry is wisdom."

And from some of them who said: "Poetry is the lowest degree of the noble, and the highest degree of the base."

And from al-Sha'bi that he said: "Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to compose poetry, ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to compose poetry, and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, was the most poetic of the three." And in some tafsirs: that His saying ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ refers to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and this is a strange opinion.

And from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud that he said: "If you see a shaykh reciting poetry in the mosque, strike his head with a staff."

As for ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas, he used to recite poetry in the mosque and ask for it to be recited to him. It is related that he summoned ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah al-Makhzumi and asked him to recite the qasidah he had recited, beginning with:

(Are you departing from the family of Naʿma, leaving in the morning, the morning after tomorrow, or returning in the evening to depart?)

So Ibn Abi Rabiʿah recited the qasidah to its end, and it was nearly seventy verses. Then Ibn ʿAbbas repeated the whole qasidah, though he had memorized it only once, and said: "I have not seen anyone more narrative-rich than ʿUmar, nor more knowledgeable than ʿAli." This account was cited by al-Mubarrad in Mushkil al-Quran.

His saying ﴿And they remember Allah much﴾ is clear in meaning.

His saying ﴿And defend themselves after being wronged﴾ means: by answering the unbelievers concerning their poetry with which they satirized the Muslims. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(You satirized Muhammad, so I answered on his behalf, and with Allah is the reward for that.)

(So my father, my mother, and my honor are a shield for the honor of Muhammad from you.)

His saying ﴿And those who wronged will know﴾ means: the unbelievers who satirized the Muslims.

His saying ﴿What return they will return to﴾ means: what place of return they will return to. And it is read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "أي منفلت ينفلتون" with the letter fa', from infilat (escape) and falling into something. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned this verse in his testament to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he appointed him as successor. It is related that he said to ʿUthman, may Allah be pleased with him: "Write: This is what Abu Bakr has bequeathed at the last of his time in this world and the first of his time in the Hereafter, when the wicked believes and the liar speaks truth. I have appointed over you ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. If he is righteous and truthful, that is my assessment of him; and if he changes and alters, I intended only good, and none knows the unseen except Allah. ﴿And those who wronged will know what return they will return to.﴾"
